name: RoMa
plain: RoMa (2024): dense matching between two photos of one scene from any viewpoints: where each pixel of the first image is in the second, and how sure the model is that it is visible there. Built on Meta's DINOv2 and a VGG19. MIT code and weights; the DINOv2 weights are Apache-2.0.
summary: RoMa (Edstedt, Sun, Bökman, Wadenbäck, Felsberg, CVPR 2024): dense feature matching between two images of any viewpoint. A frozen DINOv2 ViT-L/14 and a VGG19-BN describe both images; a Gaussian process over the coarse DINOv2 features and a transformer classifier give a coarse warp, and convolutional refiners (local correlation at strides 16, 8, 4) sharpen it at strides 16 to 1, at a coarse square size and again at a fine size. Returns, for every pixel of the first image, its position in the second (pixels) and the probability that it is visible there.
licence_notes: The DINOv2 ViT-L/14 weights are the second weight file (Meta's release, Apache-2.0).
limitations: One direction (the first image's half of upstream's symmetric call); upstream's sampling / keypoint helpers are not included; tools/eval_matching.py has the MegaDepth-1500 sampling.
Both images are resized to squares (upstream's behaviour), whatever their aspect ratio; upstream resizes PIL images, this runner float tensors (bicubic, antialiased).
task_io: Input: two RGB images of one scene. Output: for every pixel of the first image its position in the second (x, y in pixels) and a certainty that the pixel is visible in both. Sparse matchers (LightGlue) return the keypoints of both images and the index pairs of the matched ones instead.

variants.name: romav1

training_data.name: MegaDepth (Internet photo collections with SfM / MVS depth)

licence.training_note: roma_outdoor: MegaDepth (upstream README / paper). The frozen DINOv2 was pretrained on LVD-142M (not released).

variants.input_size: any H x W >= 32, padded to a multiple of 32

portable.protocol: first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

kernels.protocol: first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

original16.protocol: median of 5 after 3 warm-up, uint8 CUDA input, original code at the pinned commit, torch.no_grad; peak = max over the first call and the timed calls
original16.note: the authors' mixed-precision option (float16); upstream RoMa v1 match, one direction; local correlation: upstream's plain-torch path (use_custom_corr off)

quality.title: MegaDepth-1500, relative pose AUC@5 / @10 / @20 degrees
quality.protocol: Dense matchers: 5000 matches per pair sampled from the warp by certainty (upstream's balanced KDE sampling); sparse matchers: all their matches of one call (LightGlue, XFeat: LightGlue's MegaDepth-1500 setting; LoFTR, DeDoDe: their card defaults). OpenCV essential-matrix RANSAC (0.5 px threshold, normalised by the mean focal length); AUC of the larger of the rotation and translation-direction errors.

original16.note: upstream RoMa v1 match, amp_dtype float16 (upstream default), local correlation: upstream's plain-torch path (use_custom_corr=False)

parity.text: CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 4.3e-05 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.00079 and p99 <= 0.0042 (absolute error of the output `warp`).
